source_text: Nec nomine "sellulariorum opificum" derideas membra Christi … Quid est autem: "Quod eis cum ostendere coeperis, in me acerbiores fient"? Mentiri eis noli, et non fient. Ego enim non "eos", sicut calumniaris, "assevero peculium diaboli", quos redemptos Christi sanguine scio: "nec diabolo coniugia", in quantum coniugia sunt, "ulla transcribo"; nec "eum genitalium commentor artificem"; nec "excitatorem virorum nisi ad illicita", nec "fecundatorem mulierum", nec "conditorem" assero "parvulorum".
pass_a_gloss: Nor with the name 'of sedentary workmen' should you deride the members of Christ. But what is: 'Which when you begin to show to them, against me they will become more bitter'? Do not lie to them, and they will not become (so). For I do not 'assert them', as you slander, 'the private property of the devil', whom I know redeemed by Christ's blood: 'nor to the devil any marriages', insofar as they are marriages, 'do I transfer'; nor 'do I devise him the artificer of the genitals'; nor 'the exciter of men' except to illicit things, nor 'the fertiliser of women', nor 'the founder' do I assert 'of little ones'.

lemmas.gloss: sedentary workman, one who works sitting

pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “Do not mock the members of Christ with the name ‘sedentary craftsmen.’ … What is this: ‘When you begin to show them this, they will become more bitter toward me’? Do not lie to them, and they will not.”

“For I do not, as you falsely charge, ‘assert that they are the devil’s property,’ since I know they were redeemed by Christ’s blood; I do not ‘assign any marriages to the devil,’ insofar as they are marriages; I do not ‘make him out to be the craftsman of the genitals’; nor do I assert that he is ‘the arouser of men,’ except to unlawful acts, nor ‘the one who makes women fertile,’ nor ‘the maker of infants.’”

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
